message.content:
In Christianity, the figure most often regarded as central—and sometimes described as the ultimate prophet—is Jesus Christ. Christians believe that Jesus is the Son of God who came to fulfill the prophecies of the Hebrew Scriptures (Old Testament) and to bring salvation to humanity. Because of this belief, Jesus is seen as the culmination of prophetic revelation.

At the same time, Christianity also holds many Old Testament prophets—such as Moses, Isaiah, Jeremiah, and others—in high regard. These prophets are viewed as foretelling the coming of the Messiah and teaching moral and spiritual lessons that are foundational to Christian faith. Different Christian traditions may emphasize various aspects of prophetic history, but the consensus is that Jesus Christ occupies a unique and pivotal place in Christian theology.
